sources.title: Independent affine parameter sum
sources.details: For width w, untied embedding/output=528w; position=128w; attention=4w²; three LayerNorms=6w; each default FFN=8w²+5w. Teacher has three FFNs and router=3w; student one FFN and no router. Gives 18048 and 6104, exactly agreeing with executed parameter enumeration.

claims.statement: Output-distribution distillation can teach a Dense student from an MoE teacher without importing its experts, provided next-token candidates and conditioning positions share the same meanings.
claims.scope: Output-based distillation; no hidden-feature subtraction or equality of teacher/student capability is claimed.

evidence.supports: Knowledge viewed as input-to-output mapping; small student trained on teacher soft class distributions
Direct original-paper example of sparse-to-dense language-model distillation
Internal width/depth differ while output last axis is vocab_size
Only logits and validity labels passed; no expert identities are consumed

claims.statement: The toy teacher width16/3 experts/top2 and Dense student width8 both output (1,2,264), with total parameter counts 18048 and 6104; all three expert sets remain stored.
claims.scope: Default single-layer, one-head, untied TinyLM configurations, two input IDs; parameters are stored count, not activation cost/time.

evidence.supports: Independent affine counts including biases, embeddings, positions, norms, router and all experts
Default vocabulary 264 and exact total-parameter enumeration
Hidden width4w, all experts stored, chosen expert axis top_k=2
Four bias-free width-square projections

verification.expected: Both shapes (1,2,264); exact counts 18048/6104; three stored experts, two chosen per token
verification.observed: Original output matches; independent sums match; chosen shape (2,2)
verification.details: Axes: batch1, positions2, candidates264. Entire ModuleList counted irrespective of selected experts.
verification.tolerance: Exact integer and shape equality; no floating-point rounding involved

claims.statement: The original fence freezes the teacher and computes student KL gradients; backward alone performs no parameter update.
claims.location: 18.12 Python fence and following two paragraphs
claims.scope: Grouped ordinary APIs covered: manual_seed, tensor creation, eval, requires_grad_, no_grad, module forward/indexing, description/parameters/numel, backward, shape/tuple, abs/sum/item and print. Toy gradient path only.

evidence.supports: Original unmodified fence completed on CPU with exact displayed output
Evaluation mode and explicit teacher parameter freezing are separate operations
Teacher computation gradient recording disabled
Backward accumulates leaf gradients; this fence has no optimizer.step
Student gradient positive, teacher grads absent, every student parameter unchanged after backward

verification.expected: Student output gradient present, teacher gradients absent, no weight update
verification.observed: Gradient absolute sum 3.3217830657958984; all student weights unchanged; teacher requires_grad=False and grads None
verification.details: Original fence executed first. Separate CPU assertions compare cloned parameters before/after backward; no optimizer or checkpoint.

claims.statement: distillation_kl compares teacher||student across candidates and averages valid positions; 265 student vocabulary causes a shape error and 264 restores the route. Artificial labels only mark both positions valid.
claims.scope: This helper's shape/validity contract, temperature1; not a complete conversation mask or automatic candidate semantic remapping.

evidence.supports: Teacher detached; probabilities/log probabilities across last axis; per-token sum, valid mask and mean; rejects shape mismatch
PyTorch argument order and reduction='none' semantics
Independent formula, one-position mask, arbitrary nonignore label and exercise actually executed

verification.expected: KL equals sum p(logp-logq) averaged over two valid positions; 265 rejected and 264 accepted
verification.observed: Both manual/helper KL=0.3357211947441101; masked KL=0.36398816108703613; 265 raises ValueError; restored (1,2,264)
verification.details: Numerical formula atol1e-7/rtol1e-6. Labels 999 give unchanged KL because labels only select validity. Additional width12/layers2 variant still outputs (1,2,264).

claims.statement: Same output shape does not establish teacher skill, successful distillation, equality on all inputs or a faster Dense student; evaluation must compare a real teacher, baseline quality and measured costs.
claims.location: 18.12 random-initialization limits and final main-text paragraph
claims.scope: Qualified method restrictions and experiment design recommendations, not new empirical claims about this random teacher.

evidence.supports: Small model typically cannot exactly match all teacher soft targets

evidence.locator: Section 4.2/Table6 pp.16-17 and parallelism costs p.22
evidence.supports: Sparse-to-dense transfer measured against baselines; FLOPs, communication and memory trade-offs affect runtime
The displayed toy path has no training updates, so cannot establish learned task ability

claims.scope: Verification of recorded single-seed experiment/provenance and source operations; teacher-versus-student gap also includes data-budget differences. No historical training re-execution.

Fixed teacher export and original409-record split SHA cross-match

factual_accuracy.details: All substantive main/optional/exercise claims separately covered by original papers, personally read code contracts and recorded raw result pointers.

numeric_verification.details: Exact tensor axes/parameters/storage counts, KL denominator/mask arithmetic, original trace arithmetic and existing raw generation/nll denominators independently checked on CPU.

figure_consistency.details: 18.12 contains no referenced image. Text and executed tensors suffice for this interface/gradient example; no target figure was rendered or claimed inspected.

source_verification.details: Original Hinton v1 and Switch v3 papers personally inspected; immutable official PyTorch sources retrieved and matched to installed commit; raw recorded implementation SHA and teacher result/data/checkpoint provenance cross-matched. limitations.details: Toy proves only a differentiable interface, not learned ability. Existing result is seed42, teacher409/student32 stories and matched student objective comparison; no GPU/training/checkpoint reevaluation or original full training-data reread. No guaranteed equal capability or latency inferred.
